title: Kollar alternatives when the maximal ideal is associated modulo a regular element
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $x\in\mathfrak m$ act injectively on $R$, and suppose $\mathfrak m$ is an associated prime of $R/xR$, meaning that some nonzero class has annihilator exactly $\mathfrak m$. Then either $R$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme] of Krull dimension one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], or there exists a nonzero commutative ring $S$ and a ring map $\varphi:R\to S$, finite as an $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], not bijective, such that for some integer $n\ge1$ we have $\mathfrak m^n\ker\varphi=0$ and $\mathfrak m^n S\subseteq\varphi(R)$, and there is no $z\in S$ with $\{a\in R:\varphi(a)z=0\}=\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 0BHZ, proof fourth and fifth paragraphs (also https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BHZ)

proof.text: Use Mathlib isAssociatedPrime_iff to obtain a quotient class with annihilator the maximal ideal, and lift it to y in R. The class is nonzero because the maximal ideal is proper. Thus y is outside xR and ay lies in xR for every a in the maximal ideal.

Split on whether for every a in the maximal ideal there is b in the maximal ideal with xb = ay. In the stable subcase apply the fully proved finite-extension lemma, which constructs the subalgebra preserving the image of the maximal ideal in R localized at x.

In the other subcase select a in the maximal ideal for which no such b exists. Write ay = xc using the quotient-witness property. Then c lies outside the maximal ideal and is a unit u. Set t = u inverse times a, so yt = x and t lies in the maximal ideal. Multiplication by y is injective because multiplication by x is injective. Every b in the maximal ideal satisfies yb = xd for some d, so cancellation gives b = td. Therefore the maximal ideal equals (t). The height theorem bounds the dimension by one. Mathlib ringKrullDim_quotient_span_singleton_succ_eq_ringKrullDim applied to the regular element x bounds it below by one: R/(x) is nonzero since x lies in the proper maximal ideal, so its dimension is nonnegative. Thus the dimension is one and spanFinrank_singleton gives regularity.

Let $x\in\mathfrak m$ act injectively on $R$, and suppose $\mathfrak m$ is an associated prime of $R/xR$, meaning that some nonzero class has annihilator exactly $\mathfrak m$. Then either $R$ is a regular local ring of Krull dimension one, or there exists a nonzero commutative ring $S$ and a ring map $\varphi:R\to S$, making $S$ a finite $R$-module, not bijective, such that for some integer $n\ge1$ we have $\mathfrak m^n\ker\varphi=0$ and $\mathfrak m^n S\subseteq\varphi(R)$, and there is no $z\in S$ with $\{a\in R:\varphi(a)z=0\}=\mathfrak m$.

proof.text: By the associated-prime hypothesis there is $y\in R$ whose class in $R/xR$ is nonzero with annihilator exactly $\mathfrak m$. Thus $y\notin xR$ and $y\mathfrak m\subseteq xR$.

*Subcase $y\mathfrak m\subseteq x\mathfrak m$: property (4) with $R'=R[y/x]\subseteq R_x$.* For $f\in\mathfrak m$ write $yf=xg$ with $g\in\mathfrak m$; $g$ is unique because $x$ is a nonzerodivisor, so $\psi(f)=g$ defines a map $\psi:\mathfrak m	o\mathfrak m$, which is $R$-linear by the uniqueness. $\mathfrak m$ is a finite $R$-module since $R$ is Noetherian, so by the Cayley–Hamilton theorem for endomorphisms of finite modules (the determinant trick) there is a monic $P=T^d+a_{d-1}T^{d-1}+\cdots+a_0\in R[T]$ with $P(\psi)=0$. Let $R_x$ be the localization of $R$ at the powers of $x$. The map $R	o R_x$, $r\mapsto r/1$, is injective: $r/1=0$ means $x^kr=0$ for some $k$, so $r=0$. Put $s=y/x\in R_x$. For $f\in\mathfrak m$, $x\psi(f)=yf$ gives $\psi(f)/1=s\cdot(f/1)$, hence $\psi^i(f)/1=s^i(f/1)$ for all $i\ge0$ by induction, and $0=P(\psi)(x)/1=P(s)\cdot(x/1)$; since $x/1$ is a unit of $R_x$, $P(s)=0$.
